'''Harold Schultz Slusher''' (born 1934)<ref>{{cite book | url=https://archive.org/details/creationistsevol0000numb | url-access=registration | title=The Creationists | publisher=University of California Press | author=Numbers, Ronald L. | year=1993 | pages=[https://archive.org/details/creationistsevol0000numb/page/199 199]| isbn=9780520083936 }}</ref> is an American physicist and [[Young Earth creationism|young earth creationist]]. 

==Biography==

Slusher says he has an honorary D.Sc. from [[Indiana Christian University]] (ICU) and a Ph.D. in geophysics from [[Columbia Pacific University]]. However, according to [[Robert Schadewald]], ICU is a [[Bible college]] with no more than two people in its graduate science department, and that CPU "exhibits several qualities of a degree mill".<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.talkorigins.org/faqs/credentials.html | title=Some Questionable Creationist Credentials | work=TalkOrigins | date=31 May 2002 | accessdate=29 August 2016 | author=Vickers, Brett}}</ref>

He is assistant professor of physics at the [[University of Texas at El Paso]] and a member of the [[Institute for Creation Research]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://academics.utep.edu/default.aspx?tabid=18749 | title=Harold Slusher | work=University of Texas at El Paso | accessdate=29 August 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7ykDCAAAQBAJ | title=Diamond Dealers and Feather Merchants: Tales from the Sciences | publisher=Springer Science & Business Media | author=Klotz, Irving | year=2013 | pages=111| isbn=9781489935298 }}</ref> In 1986, [[Kendrick Frazier]] called him "perhaps the most outspoken critic of conventional science among the creationists".<ref>{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=i2Nm8OyXpyQC | title=Science Confronts the Paranormal | publisher=Prometheus Books | author=Frazier, Kendrick | year=1986 | pages=314| isbn=9781615926190 }}</ref>

Slusher believes the earth is 7000 to 10,000 years old.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Klotz, Irving M|year=1982|title=Commentary: Why Not Teach Creationism in the Schools? |journal=[[BioScience]]|volume=32|issue=5|pages=334–335|doi=10.2307/1308851 |jstor=1308851 }}</ref> He is an opponent of Albert Einstein's [[theory of relativity]].<ref>[https://ncse.ngo/files/pub/library/Theses/McIver,%20Tom%20-%20Creationism%20-%20Intellectual%20Origins,%20Cultural%20Context,%20and%20Theoretical%20Diversity.pdf "Creationism: Intellectual Origins, Cultural Context, and Theoretical Diversity"]. Thomas Allen McIver, 1989.</ref>

==''Biology: A Search for Order in Complexity''==

In 1974, Slusher co-edited the revised edition of the creationist textbook for students, ''Biology: A Search for Order in Complexity''.<ref name="Simpson 1975">{{cite journal|author=Simpson, Ronald D; Anderson, Wyatt W.|year=1975|title=Reviewed Work: SAME SONG, SECOND VERSE—A Review of Biology: A Search for Order in Complexity, Revised Edition by John N. Moore, Harold Schultz Slusher|journal=[[The Science Teacher]]|volume=42|issue=5|pages=40–42}}</ref> The textbook was developed by the [[Creation Research Society]] and published by [[Zondervan]]. It was negatively reviewed as a pseudoscientific textbook that misrepresents biological evolution.<ref name="Simpson 1975"/><ref>{{cite journal|author=Mariner, James L; McBurney, Wendell F.|year=1971|title=Reviewed Work: Biology: A Search for Order in Complexity by John N. Moore, Harold Schultz Slusher|journal=[[The American Biology Teacher]]|volume=33|issue=7|pages=438–442|doi=10.2307/4443635 |jstor=4443635 }}</ref><ref>[https://ncse.ngo/review-biology-search-order-complexity "Review: Biology: A Search for Order in Complexity"]. National Center for Science Education. Retrieved 30 January 2021.</ref> A negative review in ''[[The Science Teacher]]'' noted that the "text grossly distorts the biological theory of evolution, so much that it is barely recognizable".<ref name="Simpson 1975"/> The textbook does not define [[natural selection]] and falsely leads its readers to "believe that evolution is the result of chance mutation, when in fact it is the result of selection acting on genetic variability which arises ultimately by mutation. The picture of evolution presented in this book is wrong and flagrantly so".<ref name="Simpson 1975"/> The review also noted that the textbook falsely defines evolution as the "ameba to man" theory where organisms of one "[[Created kind|kind]]" change into another "kind".<ref name="Simpson 1975"/> In 1977, an Indiana state [[superior court]] determined that the use of the textbook is unconstitutional (see [[Hendren v. Campbell]]).<ref>''Hendren v. Campbell''. 1977. Marion County Superior Court. No. 5, Indiana. Case No. S577-0139.</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Fowler, Dean R.|year=1982|title=The Creationist Movement|journal=[[The American Biology Teacher]]|volume=44|issue=9|pages=528–542|doi=10.2307/4447600 |jstor=4447600 }}</ref>

==Selected publications==

*''Critique of Radiometric Dating'' (1973)
*''Biology: A Search for Order in Complexity'' (with John N. Moore, 1974)
*''Origin of the Universe'' (1980)
*''Motion of Mercury's Perihelion'' (with Francisco Ramirez, 1984)
